title: Recording: Silly Love Songs by Wings | 1976
content:
Studio Three, Abbey Road Studios, London
Producer: Paul McCartney
Engineer: Peter Henderson

Wings continued work on the Wings At The Speed Of Sound song ‘Silly Love Songs’ on 20 February 1976.

The session lasted from 7.30-11pm, and saw Paul McCartney re-record his lead vocals. He used EMI’s ADT (artificial double-tracking) to give the effect of two vocal parts. ADT had been developed and first used during the sessions for The Beatles’ Revolver.

Wings’ horn section – Howie Casey on saxophone, Tony Dorsey on trombone, and Steve Howard and Thaddeus Richard on flugelhorn – were also recorded. McCartney showed the musicians what he wanted on the piano, and they worked out the arrangement during the session.

Paul has absolute control of all of his music. I think he basically likes to have have someone to critique his work to reassure him. Occasionally he would come to me and say, ‘I need horns here, but I have no idea, so give me your best shot.’ Or, like on ‘Silly Love Songs’, he knew exactly what he wanted from the horns but had no idea what he wanted from the strings.
Tony Dorsey
